transport: RS-485 RJ-45 (jacks "COMM 1" / "COMM 2") · Modbus RTU · baud unknown · slave ID = "COMM ID" parameter, range 1-255, default 1
blocks: Same NDA wall as the 22xx/40xx dialect, and worse: no community implementation covers the 4248SP at all, so there is not even a baud rate for it. Nothing exists to build from.
gotchas: KEPT SEPARATE FROM THE 22xx/40xx DIALECT DELIBERATELY. The EVO-RC-PLUS manual gives the 4248SP its own data-logging figure (§5.2.2.3, Fig 5.3) with a materially different field set from Fig 5.2 — dual-leg output/input, CAN status, CAN watt, AVG watt, two heat-sink sensors, and no busbar temperature. Different telemetry
No baud rate from any source for this model. Do not carry 9600 over from the 22xx dialect — that would be interpolation.
Modbus presence is vendor-doc: docs/samlex-evo-4248sp-manual-fw0.77.pdf Fig 2.1 legend items 9a/9b, identical wording to the 22xx manual.
This is the only 48 V, 120/240 V split-phase model in the Samlex line and the one most likely to be the whole-cabin inverter, which makes the missing map the most expensive gap on this page.
unmappedReports: Split-phase L1/L2 dimension — the vendor logs 'Output watt 1'/'Output watt 2', 'Output VA 1'/'2', 'Output Amp 1'/'2', 'Input Amp 1'/'2', 'Input VA 1'/'2', 'Input watt 1'/'2'. MetricKind has no per-leg or per-phase qualifier. A 120/240 V unit reports every AC quantity twice and the contract can hold one of them., 'CAN status' and 'CAN watt' — 4248SP-only fields, present in no other EVO model's log. Suggests a CAN-attached device (BMS? second unit?) whose power the 4248SP reports. Undocumented in the owner's manual, which calls COMM 3/COMM 4 'for future use'., 'AVG watt' — averaged output power, 4248SP-only., AC input side, 'Grid status', 'Grid freq', 'External Amp', 'Mode', 'Error code', 'Event', 'Fan speed', 'Transformer (c)', 'Heat sink 1 (c)', 'Heat sink 2 (c)' — same gaps as the 22xx/40xx dialect.
